plates.title: Map of the Relational World
plates.prompt: An antique hand-drawn map in sepia ink and faded color washes on aged parchment, depicting a journey of territories connected by dotted trade-routes, in the style of a 17th-century cartographer's illustrated atlas page. At the top, a worried traveller stands at a signpost crossroads looking toward distant mechanical figures laboring in a factory-shaped region, two faint ghostly cheering hands floating above him, titled TWO CHEERS, UNEASY. Three roads lead down and outward to three walled territories drawn side by side: first, a gilded palace region where courtiers argue over a heraldic emblem while an unattended stage sits empty, titled PALACE OF PRECEDENCE; second, a manor region where well-dressed women sit at a long table with seating cards and ledgers, a mansion looming behind, titled LADIES WHO LUNCH; third, a crowded tenement region at night where men and women gather around a table gambling and talking, work-clothes hanging unused by the door, titled THE URBAN VILLAGERS. Beneath the palace territory, a smaller inset shows a powdered courtier standing beside a chained ape mirroring his posture, both inside a drawn cage of tiny rule-tablets, titled COURT AS CAGE. Beneath the manor territory, a woman at a podium casts a hollow empty shadow on the wall, titled ILLUSION OF USE. Beneath the tenement territory, a wrecking ball swings into the building as former neighbors flee with bundles and a condominium rises behind, titled THE WEST END FALLS. All three routes converge at the center of the map on a shared circular plaza where three separate walled circles of tiny figures meet around one carved crest, titled THE CLANNISH PATTERN. From this plaza a single road continues downward to a workshop region: a worker at a bench holds up a finished object to approving onlookers, no crest or banner nearby, titled RESPECT FOR THE WORK. Beside it, a procession of different tradesfolk — waitress, sommelier, clerk — each hold a tool of their trade and smile, titled WHAT WORK GIVES BACK. The road ends at the bottom of the map where the original worried traveller reappears beside a loom weaving two threads, one marked with a tiny padlock and one with a tiny open hand, looking back up toward the distant machines, titled THE LOOM OF BOTH. Compass rose and sea-serpent flourishes may fill empty corners sparingly; no lettering anywhere except the vignette titles.

plates.title: The Court Territory, Enlarged
plates.prompt: An antique hand-drawn map inset, in the same sepia ink and faded washes as a cartographer's atlas page, zooming into the court territory of the larger map. At the top, a grand candlelit palace hall glitters with courtiers in fine dress beneath a floating laurel wreath, titled VERSAILLES AT ITS HEIGHT. Below, two dukes argue fiercely over a feathered ceremonial hat held between them, genealogy scrolls scattered at their feet, titled THE DISPUTED HEADGEAR. Beside this, a drawing-room salon shows chattering guests behind fans while a philosopher's book lies closed and unread on a side table, titled SALON WITHOUT PHILOSOPHY. Tucked beside the salon as a small marginal inset, a historian at a writing desk surrounded by stacked memoirs points between two identical open pages, titled LILTI'S FINDING. Further down, a St. Petersburg court scene shows whispering courtiers leaning together behind a throne where a stern empress sits, titled CATHERINE'S COURT. Below that, a proud nobleman stands beside a stone family crest, turning his back on a tradesman who offers a crafted object, titled HONOR OVER DILIGENCE. Next, a row of posturing courtiers eyeing one another's rank is drawn directly beside a troop of apes in the same dominance poses, titled RANK ON DISPLAY. At the bottom of the plate, the palace appears crumbling into ruin at one edge while a fresh green path leads away from it toward open, undrawn land, titled A SANER STARTING POINT. The vignettes are arranged in a flowing vertical chain with thin dotted connecting routes as on a map, large enough to read clearly, filling the width of the page with sparse decorative border flourishes only in empty corners. No lettering anywhere except the vignette titles.

plates.title: The Workshop Territory, Enlarged
plates.prompt: An antique hand-drawn map inset, in the same sepia ink and faded washes as a cartographer's atlas page, zooming into the workshop territory of the larger map. At the top center, a worker displays a finished piece of work to a gathered crowd of varied trades, with no family crest or banner among them, titled DIGNITY FROM THE WORK. Branching from this hub in four directions: a long tally board shows rows of small figures at their trades, most marked with a tiny smiling face beside a counting tally, titled MOST ARE SATISFIED; a line of workers of very different trades stand scowling, each with a small mechanical gear pinned mockingly to their coat, titled TREATED LIKE A ROBOT; a bartender in an apron stands before a shuttered casino speaking to a reporter with a notebook, titled WE WANT TO FEEL USEFUL; and an elderly figure recounts their life story to a seated writer with a notebook, a small remembered scene of tools and a handshake drawn above them, titled A LIFE STORY TOLD. These four routes converge lower on the page at a walled gate where a gatekeeper figure turns away a stranger while a huddled group remains inside, titled POLICING THE GATE. From the gate, a path leads to an open market square where two friends shake hands freely with no coin or contract between them, a gate standing open behind them, titled FRIENDSHIP SET FREE. At the bottom of the plate, a solitary figure sits at a workbench looking toward a horizon where both a workshop and a walled garden are visible, one hand resting hopefully on the bench, titled A WARY HOPE. Vignettes connected by thin dotted map-routes, arranged to fill the width of the page, large and clear, with only sparse border flourishes in empty corners. No lettering anywhere except the vignette titles.
